blueprint.source: CNCF / Linux Foundation CKA curriculum: Troubleshooting 30% · Cluster Architecture, Installation & Configuration 25% · Services & Networking 20% · Workloads & Scheduling 15% · Storage 10%
blueprint.mapping: each CKA drill → one official domain (ILImmersiveExam.BLUEPRINT / OFFICIAL)
blueprint.score: per official domain on the finished paper; blueprint-weighted % renormalised over the domains the paper covered (coverage % shown; untested domains listed, never counted as passed)
blueprint.weakest: domain with the most points at stake = weight × (1 − score); links to that domain's 3D drill
blueprint.honesty: Published CKA weights over this device's answers on in-browser 3D drills — a study signal, not a predicted CNCF exam score. Troubleshooting is covered by three drills since 2026-10-23 (control-plane-failure, node-troubleshoot, service-dns).

review.scheduler: Leitner boxes 0-6 (0, 10m, 1d, 3d, 7d, 16d, 35d); miss -> box 0; correct slower than 45s holds box; correct first sighting on exam -> box 2
feeds: exam papers (/immersive/exam/, incl. timeouts as misses)
CLI-lab steps the Lab Muse coach had to rescue (`solution` or 2 failed checks) — since 2026-10-20
review.mastery: avg box / 6 over every CKA checkpoint in domain; unseen = 0
review.honesty: On-device spaced repetition over the in-browser 3D rules engine. Not FSRS, not a trained model, no server or cohort data, not a live cluster.
review.cliCards: kind 'cli' cards re-open the CLI task step on the authored stage (review runtime v1.2.0)
review.blueprint: since 2026-10-21: /immersive/review/ shows mastery per official CKA domain, weighted by the published exam weights (unseen checkpoints = 0), with the weakest domain by points at stake; Lab Muse names it when read aloud

webxr.entry: Enter VR / Enter AR on every ScenePlayer stage (free-play, /immersive/exam/, /immersive/review/) — shown only when navigator.xr.isSessionSupported() is true; hidden without WebXR and under prefers-reduced-motion

In-headset predict HUD is local WebGL UI (not Unreal UMG / Pixel Streaming HUD). Verified in CI against a scripted navigator.xr fake (headless Chromium has no XR device), not a physical headset.

hud.honesty: Local WebGL/WebXR UI over authored glTF — not Unreal UMG, not a Pixel Streaming HUD, not a hosted cluster.

cli.verify: Killercoda-style tasks: goal → ordered steps (event steps must follow the previous event step; state steps are checked live) → complete
ux: check (and a Check button) · hint · solution · task · reset · clear · help
analytics: immersive_cli_cmd (verb + exit code only, never the raw command text)
immersive_cli_coach (action + level + step index only, never command text)
immersive_cli_review_card (sim + task + step index + why: solution | check-fail — never command text)
immersive_cli_voice (sim + kind: verb | command | none | error + ok — never the transcript)
cli.storage: localStorage il.immersiveCli.v1 (task completions + best command count, device only); CLI review cards in il.immersiveReview.v1 (device only)
cli.honesty: Simulated shell over the in-browser rules engine — real CLI syntax, computed output (kubectl/etcdctl/aws-shaped, not byte-identical). Not a real shell, container, cluster, AWS account or hosted lab fleet. Unmodelled commands say so instead of inventing output.

coach.benchmark: Killercoda Brain (2026): hint vs solution mode, hint offered after the 2nd failed verification, explains why a solution is not accepted
coach.ladder: check #1 on a step → diagnosis · check #2+ → diagnosis + tip (never the command) · solution → exact command
diagnosis: out of order (seen before the previous step verified)
right command family, wrong cluster state
coach.spatial: each step names authored glTF nodes (focus regex, unit-tested against the .glb); the player pulses them gold for ~9 s — also in WebXR; static stages list them
coach.voice: optional 'Lab Muse voice' toggle — browser speechSynthesis only (no cloud TTS, no key); hidden when unavailable
coach.honesty: Deterministic rules over the same in-browser sim state — not an LLM, not reading a real terminal, knows only what the drill models.

cli.ingressNote: ingress-nginx was retired 2026-03-24; the Ingress API stays GA and Gateway API is the successor. The ingress pack covers the Ingress API only.

reviewCards.trigger: a free-play step where you typed `solution`, or failed `check` on it twice, becomes one spaced-repetition card (once per step per session)
reviewCards.store: the existing il.immersiveReview.v1 Leitner queue (key sim::cli:task:step); due CLI cards are served, never used as top-ups; domain mastery stays on predict checkpoints
reviewCards.review: /immersive/review/ re-mounts the drill's authored .glb with the simulated shell, replays the earlier steps from their own solutions, and grades the target step: verified without `solution` = recalled; `solution` / give-up = miss (box 0)
reviewCards.honesty: On-device Leitner scheduling — not FSRS, not a trained model, no server.

voice.api: Web Speech SpeechRecognition / webkitSpeechRecognition (feature-checked; the Speak button is hidden when unsupported)
voice.behaviour: lab verbs (check, hint, solution, task, reset, clear, help) run directly; spoken commands are normalised ("dash n" → -n, "dot" → ., snapped to this drill's vocabulary) into the input for you to check and press Enter — never auto-run
voice.honesty: Uses the browser's own speech recognition (some browsers send audio to their vendor's speech service). Interstitium receives no audio or transcript. Not an LLM.

cli.gatewayNote: Gateway API pack (2026-10-21) drives the gateway-api sim on the same authored ingress-gateway.glb. GatewayClass lab-gw (controllerName example.net/lab-gateway-controller) is a lab implementation computed by the rules engine — not Envoy Gateway, Istio, Cilium or NGINX Gateway Fabric, and not a live Gateway.
cli.nodeNote: Worker-node pack (2026-10-22) drives node-troubleshoot on the NEW authored node-troubleshoot.glb. systemd, journald, crictl, df and sed output is computed from sim state (shaped like the real tools, not byte-identical; journal lines are labelled representative). No VM, no real kubelet, no clock: durations such as node-monitor-grace-period and the 300s eviction toleration are explained, not simulated.
cli.serviceDnsNote: Service + DNS pack (2026-10-23) drives service-dns on the NEW authored service-dns.glb. Lookups go through the rules engine's resolv.conf model (search shop.svc.cluster.local svc.cluster.local cluster.local, ndots:5) over four cluster records; nslookup / dig / CoreDNS log output is shaped like the real tools (labelled representative), not byte-identical. No live cluster, no real CoreDNS, no internet upstream, no clock: CrashLoopBackOff back-off and resolver timeouts are explained, not counted down. Files written with `>` live only in this terminal session.
cli.cniNote: CNI pack (2026-10-27) drives cni-network on the authored cni-pod-network.glb (no new asset). Calico is the modelled CNI; calico.yaml and new-pool.yaml are trimmed lab stand-ins, and kubectl get/patch ippool stands in for calicoctl or the Calico API server (projectcalico.org/v3). The pool migration follows Calico's documented order (create the new pool, disable the old one, recreate pods). ping / curl / nslookup results are computed from the rules engine, shaped like busybox and curl output, not byte-identical. No live cluster, no real Calico, no VPC routing, no clock.
cli.meshNote: Service-mesh pack (2026-10-27) drives mesh-mtls on the authored service-mesh-sidecar.glb (no new asset). Istio semantics: STRICT resets plaintext clients, injection needs the namespace label and newly created pods, PERMISSIVE accepts both, istiod at zero leaves existing sidecars on their last config while the sidecar-injector webhook (failurePolicy Fail) blocks new pods. payments echoes headers like httpbin /headers, so X-Forwarded-Client-Cert shows an mTLS hop. istioctl output is computed and trimmed. Not CKA core; no live mesh, no real Envoy or istiod.
